message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of a few popular services that let you look up business‑level data (company name, industry, size, etc.) and optionally pull out contact details such as email addresses or phone numbers: | Service | Key Features | Free Tier / Pricing | How to Call | |---------|--------------|---------------------|-------------| | **ipinfo.io** | • Company name, domain, AS, city, region, postal code, timezone
• “Company” field includes `name`, `domain`, `industry`, `size`
• Optional “contact” sub‑object (email, phone) via paid plan | $50/month for 50k queries + 10k “business” queries per month; free tier limited to 1k monthly requests, no contact data | `https://ipinfo.io//json?token=` | | **ipapi.co** | • Organization name, ASN, carrier, domain, organization type
• “org” field gives company name; “asn_org” gives org name
• Contact fields only in paid plans | $45/month for 25k requests + 5k “business” queries; free tier 30k/month but no contact data | `https://ipapi.co//json/?key=` | | **ipstack.com** | • Company name, domain, industry, employee count, revenue range
• “company” object contains `name`, `domain`, `industry`, `size`, `revenue_range`
• Contact info (phone, email) in higher tiers | $99/month for 500k requests + 20k “business” queries; free tier 10k/month, no contact data | `http://api.ipstack.com/?access_key=&format=1&fields=ip,company` | | **Clearbit Enrichment** | • Very detailed company profile (employees, funding, social links)
• Email lookup via Clearbit Connect (requires separate product) | Pay-as-you-go ($0.01/query after first 200 free); requires OAuth & API key | `https://person.clearbit.com/v2/combined/find?ip=` (needs auth) | ### Quick Example – Using ipinfo.io ```python import requests def get_company_info(ip_address): url = f"https://ipinfo.io/{ip_address}/json" params = {"token": "YOUR_IPINFO_TOKEN"} # replace with your actual token resp = requests.get(url, params=params, timeout=5) if resp.status_code != 200: raise Exception(f"Error {resp.status_code}: {resp.text}") data = resp.json() result = { "ip": data.get("ip"), "city": data.get("city"), "region": data.get("region"), "country": data.get("country"), "postal": data.get("postal"), "timezone": data.get("timezone"), "company_name": None, "company_domain": None, "company_industry": None, "company_size": None, "contact_email": None, "contact_phone": None, } company = data.get("company") if company: result["company_name"] = company.get("name") result["company_domain"] = company.get("domain") result["company_industry"] = company.get("industry") result["company_size"] = company.get("size") # Some providers expose a nested “contact” object contact = data.get("contact") or data.get("company", {}).get("contact") if contact: result["contact_email"] = contact.get("email") result["contact_phone"] = contact.get("phone") return result print(get_company_info("8.8.8.8")) ``` Replace `"YOUR_IPINFO_TOKEN"` with the token you receive when you sign up at [ipinfo.io](https://ipinfo.io/signup). The free tier will give you basic location and company name data; to get the `contact` sub‑object you’ll need to upgrade to a paid plan. ### Things to Keep in Mind 1. **Rate Limits** – All services impose limits on free usage. Exceeding those limits will either throttle you or return errors until you upgrade. 2. **Privacy & Compliance** – Make sure you’re compliant with GDPR, CCPA, etc., especially if you store personal contact info. Many APIs include a disclaimer that the data is sourced from publicly available records and may not be fully accurate. 3. **Data Accuracy** – Contact emails and phone numbers are often scraped from the web and can become stale quickly. Consider adding a “last verified” timestamp if you cache the results. 4. **Caching Strategy** – For high‑volume systems, cache the API responses (e.g., Redis or local memory) keyed by IP address. Invalidate after a reasonable period (e.g., 24–48 h) because corporate ownership can change. 5. **Fallbacks** – If the chosen provider doesn’t return contact data, you can fall back to other enrichment services (e.g., Clearbit, FullContact) or try reverse‑lookup on the domain returned (`company.domain`) to fetch email patterns.
